<p dir="auto">Uvicorn is an ASGI web server implementation for Python.</p>
<p dir="auto">
Until recently Python has lacked a minimal low-level server/application interface for
async frameworks. The 
<a href="https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/" rel="nofollow">ASGI specification</a>
 fills this gap, and means we're now able to
start building a common set of tooling usable across all async frameworks.
</p>
<p dir="auto">Uvicorn supports HTTP/1.1 and WebSockets.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

<p dir="auto">This will install uvicorn with "Cython-based" dependencies (where possible) and other "optional extras".</p>
<p dir="auto">In this context, "Cython-based" means the following:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
the event loop 
<code>uvloop</code>
 will be installed and used if possible.
</li>
<li>
the http protocol will be handled by 
<code>httptools</code>
 if possible.
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Moreover, "optional extras" means that:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
the websocket protocol will be handled by 
<code>websockets</code>
 (should you want to use 
<code>wsproto</code>
 you'd need to install it manually) if possible.
</li>
<li>
the 
<code>--reload</code>
 flag in development mode will use 
<code>watchfiles</code>
.
</li>
<li>
<code>python-dotenv</code>
 will be installed should you want to use the 
<code>--env-file</code>
 option.
</li>
<li>
<code>PyYAML</code>
 will be installed to allow you to provide a 
<code>.yaml</code>
 file to 
<code>--log-config</code>
, if desired.
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">
Create an application, in 
<code>example.py</code>
:
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">app</span>
(
<span class="pl-s1">scope</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">receive</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">send</span>
):
    
<span class="pl-k">assert</span> <span class="pl-s1">scope</span>
[
<span class="pl-s">'type'</span>
] 
<span class="pl-c1">==</span> <span class="pl-s">'http'</span>

    <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">send</span>
({
        
<span class="pl-s">'type'</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">'http.response.start'</span>
,
        
<span class="pl-s">'status'</span>
: 
<span class="pl-c1">200</span>
,
        
<span class="pl-s">'headers'</span>
: [
            (
<span class="pl-s">b'content-type'</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">b'text/plain'</span>
),
        ],
    })
    
<span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">send</span>
({
        
<span class="pl-s">'type'</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">'http.response.body'</span>
,
        
<span class="pl-s">'body'</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">b'Hello, world!'</span>
,
    })
</pre>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">
<h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why ASGI?</h2>
<a id="user-content-why-asgi" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why ASGI?" href="#why-asgi">
<svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true">
<path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path>
</svg>
</a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">Most well established Python Web frameworks started out as WSGI-based frameworks.</p>
<p dir="auto">WSGI applications are a single, synchronous callable that takes a request and returns a response.
This doesn’t allow for long-lived connections, like you get with long-poll HTTP or WebSocket connections,
which WSGI doesn't support well.</p>
<p dir="auto">Having an async concurrency model also allows for options such as lightweight background tasks,
and can be less of a limiting factor for endpoints that have long periods being blocked on network
I/O such as dealing with slow HTTP requests.</p>
<hr>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">
<h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Alternative ASGI servers</h2>
<a id="user-content-alternative-asgi-servers" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Alternative ASGI servers" href="#alternative-asgi-servers">
<svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true">
<path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path>
</svg>
</a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">A strength of the ASGI protocol is that it decouples the server implementation
from the application framework. This allows for an ecosystem of interoperating
webservers and application frameworks.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">
<h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Daphne</h3>
<a id="user-content-daphne" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Daphne" href="#daphne">

<p dir="auto">
The first ASGI server implementation, originally developed to power Django Channels, is 
<a href="https://github.com/django/daphne">the Daphne webserver</a>
.
</p>
<p dir="auto">It is run widely in production, and supports HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and WebSockets.</p>
<p dir="auto">
Any of the example applications given here can equally well be run using 
<code>daphne</code>
 instead.
</p>

<p dir="auto">
<a href="https://github.com/pgjones/hypercorn">Hypercorn</a>
 was initially part of the Quart web framework, before
being separated out into a standalone ASGI server.
</p>
<p dir="auto">Hypercorn supports HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and WebSockets.</p>
<p dir="auto">
It also supports 
<a href="https://trio.readthedocs.io" rel="nofollow">
the excellent 
<code>trio</code>
 async framework
</a>
, as an alternative to 
<code>asyncio</code>
.
</p>
